about: Dómine, non sum dignus adapts the centurion's words in Matthew 8:8, replacing puer meus — my servant — with ánima mea — my soul. Panem cæléstem accípiam likewise adapts Psalm 115:4 in the Vulgate (Psalm 116:13 in Hebrew numbering): Cálicem salutáris accípiam — I will take the chalice of salvation. The priest repeats Dómine, non sum dignus three times, beginning each invocation in a slightly raised voice and continuing quietly.

s01.narrative: The priest genuflects, rises, and says:

s02.translation: I will receive the Bread of heaven and call upon the name of the Lord.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s03.narrative: Bowing a little, the priest takes both halves of the Host in his left hand and slips the paten beneath them. Striking his breast three times with his right hand, he says the following three times in a slightly raised voice, devoutly and humbly:

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s06.translation: that You should enter under my roof: but only say the word, and my soul shall be healed.

s13.narrative: The priest signs himself with the Host over the paten, and says:

s14.translation: May the Body of our Lord Jesus Christ preserve my soul for eternal life. Amen.

s15.narrative: Bowing, the priest reverently receives both halves of the Host, lays the paten on the corporal, joins his hands and rests a while in meditation on the Most Holy Sacrament.
